newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Bank executive charged with insider trading.
newsitem.headline: Bank executive charged with insider trading.

text.p: The Australian Securities Commission (ASC) said on Monday that Macquarie Bank Ltd (MBL) executive director Simon Hannes had been charged with one count of insider trading over trade in options to buy TNT Ltd shares in September last year ahead of a takeover bid.

"On the information presently available to the ASC, the ASC holds no suspicion that anyone else from MBL is involved in any of the matters alleged against Mr Hannes," the corporate regulator said in a statement.

Macquarie Bank was the adviser to TNT on the successful A$2 billion (US$1.5 million) takeover bid for the Australian-based global transport group by the Dutch telecommunications and postal group, Koninklijke PTT Nederland NV (KPN).
The charge followed investigations into trading in call options to buy TNT shares before the A$2.45 a share takeover bid by KPN was launched on October 2 last year.
"The prompt completion of this part of the ASC's investigation was assisted by co-operation from Macquarie," the ASC said.
"It is alleged that Mr Hannes had possession of price sensitive information about the takeover at the time he purchased, or procured the purchase of A$2 November 1996 TNT call options."
The ASC said the matter had been stood over until June 10.

The ASC laid charges of failing to report financial transactions against Hannes on January 20, but stopped short of full insider trading charges. Hannes has pleaded not guilty to the previous charges.
Hannes is a senior executive of the bank's corporate advisory division, but was not part of the team working on the TNT transaction, Macquarie said in January.
Hannes had been on extended leave at the time of the TNT bid but was available for part-time consultation.

Hannes was named in court in February as the fictitious TNT options trader Mark Booth, who would have made a A$2 million profit after buying about A$90,000 of the TNT options if the ASC had not moved to block the transaction.
Hannes was alleged to have withdrawn sums of A$9,900 or less from his bank accounts and then paid them into an account in the name of M. Booth.
A financial transaction must be reported under Australia's Financial Transactions Reports Act if above A$10,000.
Hannes was charged with trying to avoid reporting the transaction.
TNT's shares were trading around A$1.60 at the time of the A$2.45 bid.
